mainEntity.name: What is the best window management app for Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rectangle is the strongest free and open-source dedicated option. Magnet is a simple paid snapping tool. BetterTouchTool is best for custom gestures and automation. Raycast fits keyboard-first command users. Gojo fits people who want window controls inside a broader MacBook notch workspace.

mainEntity.name: Do Mac window managers need Accessibility permission?

acceptedAnswer.text: Window managers commonly need macOS Accessibility permission to move, resize, focus, or inspect windows. The exact prompt depends on the app and feature. Review the permission request before granting it and remove access when you stop using the app.

mainEntity.name: Is Gojo a replacement for Rectangle?

acceptedAnswer.text: Gojo can replace a basic snapping workflow when you also want clipboard, files, media, dictation, and other notch controls. Rectangle remains the better fit for a dedicated window manager with a broader published shortcut and snap-area system.

blocks.text: How to evaluate a Mac window manager

content.s: Start with the action you repeat: snap left or right, maximize, move between displays, restore a layout, or switch windows. Then check how you trigger it. A dedicated tool may offer more shortcuts and snap areas. A command launcher may keep the action in a keyboard search. A gesture tool may let the trackpad or mouse do the work. Also check Accessibility permission, multi-monitor behavior, fullscreen edge cases, and whether the app becomes another permanent control surface to maintain.

blocks.text: 1. Gojo for window controls without another specialist app

content.s: Gojo puts window previews, focus, organization, and quick snapping in the same notch surface as clipboard history, file staging, media, local dictation, and display controls. This works well when your window problem is part of a larger interruption pattern. It is not the specialist choice for complex saved layouts or a large catalog of custom snap targets. Window operations use Accessibility-trusted operations, and some apps or windows can limit what macOS allows Gojo to move or resize.

items: Gojo requires macOS Accessibility permission for window operations.
Gojo's public feature description promises preview, focus, organize, and quick snapping, not a saved-layout manager.
Gojo is designed for MacBook owners who want several daily controls in one surface.

content.s: Rectangle's official site says the free app is open source, supports macOS 10.15 and later, and moves and resizes windows with keyboard shortcuts or snap areas. Rectangle Pro is a separate closed-source superset with custom size and position, layouts, snap panels, quick throw, stash, and other power-user features. Choose Rectangle when snapping is the job. It is easier to justify than a broader utility if you do not want other modules.

blocks.text: 3. Magnet for a simple paid snap tool

content.s: Magnet is a familiar paid Mac App Store option for arranging windows while multitasking. Its exact current layouts, shortcut set, permission prompts, and regional price should be checked in the live listing before purchase. That limited public evidence is why this article does not assign Magnet a feature count or a price claim. It is a sensible candidate when you want an app-store snap utility and do not need a wider workspace.

Raycast's pricing page includes Window Management in its free core feature set, with Custom Window Management Commands listed under Pro. That is a good fit if you already open Raycast to launch apps, search extensions, run snippets, or control your Mac. It is a different interaction from Gojo's hoverable notch surface. Raycast wins when the keyboard is the home of your workflow; Gojo wins when glanceable controls should stay visible near the top of the screen.

blocks.text: 5. BetterTouchTool for custom input and automation

content.s: BetterTouchTool's official feature page documents drag-to-snap, custom snap areas on any display, a customizable window switcher, keyboard and modifier actions, and hundreds of trigger types. It is the strongest choice here for someone who wants to design the trigger as carefully as the result. That control takes setup. If you want a ready-made notch workflow, Gojo has fewer decisions to configure.

items.q: What is the best window management app for Mac?

a.s: Rectangle is the strongest free, open-source dedicated choice. BetterTouchTool is strongest for custom gestures and automation. Raycast fits launcher users. Gojo fits a wider MacBook notch workflow that includes window controls.

items.q: Do Mac window managers need Accessibility permission?

a.s: Apps that move, resize, focus, or inspect windows commonly need Accessibility permission. Review the exact features you are enabling, and remove access when you uninstall or stop using the tool.

items.q: Is Gojo a replacement for Rectangle?

a.s: Gojo can cover basic snapping when you also want clipboard, files, media, dictation, and other notch tools. Rectangle remains the better fit for dedicated shortcut and snap-area depth.

items.q: Can I use Gojo and Rectangle together?

a.s: Yes. Rectangle can own detailed snapping while Gojo handles the rest of the notch workspace. Avoid assigning conflicting shortcuts and review both apps' Accessibility permissions.
